task: Keep the global Proof-or-Stop executable working after dist rebuilds and make its diagnostics and evidence portable across POSIX and Windows hosts.
outcome: After npm --prefix packages/main run build, the red regression prints "contract: global-cli-bin-target-restored" and proof-or-stop --version succeeds; proof-or-stop doctor prints "contract: global-core-realpath-pass" with the compiled version, or version=unknown when that probe fails.
facts: TypeScript emits fresh POSIX dist entrypoints without executable bits.
The global executable may be a symlink or npm command shim targeting packages/main/dist/cli.js, so promotion must preserve the host-specific executable contract.
promoteDist validates and restores staging bin targets before evicting the working dist.
Final symlinks and intermediate-directory symlink escapes must not be followed by chmod.
POSIX validates executable mode bits; Windows validates the byte-identical Node entrypoint and npm-generated command shim rather than POSIX mode bits.
A failed compiled-version probe is not evidence for the package manifest version.
constraints: Use only node: built-ins in scripts/promote-dist.mjs.
Preserve atomic promotion and leave the old dist intact when staging validation fails.
Treat only ENOENT as a benign absent-target condition.
Doctor remains read-only and must emit remediation executable by the current host shell.
Story metadata and implementation remain English.
